subject: general
question: Prabhdeep buys 60 identical pens for ₹900. She sells 45 of them at a profit of 20% and the remaining at a loss of 40%. What is the total profit or loss percentage on the whole transaction?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

CP per pen = 900 ÷ 60 = 15

45 pens at 20% profit ⇒ SP = 45 × 18 = 810

15 pens at 40% loss ⇒ SP = 15 × 9 = 135

Total SP = 945, CP = 900

**∴ Answer = 5% profit**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total pens = 60, Total CP = 900

45 pens sold at 20% profit, remaining 15 at 40% loss

**Formula used:**

SP = CP × (1 ± Profit/Loss%)

**Calculation:**

⇒ CP per pen = 900 ÷ 60 = 15

⇒ SP of 45 pens at 20% profit = 45 × (15 × 1.2)

⇒ = 45 × 18 = 810

⇒ SP of 15 pens at 40% loss = 15 × (15 × 0.6)

⇒ = 15 × 9 = 135

⇒ Total SP = 810 + 135 = 945

⇒ Total CP = 900

⇒ Profit = 945 − 900 = 45

⇒ Profit% = (45 ÷ 900) × 100

⇒ = 5%

**∴ The correct answer is 5% profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit Formula

SP = CP × (1 + Profit%)

Loss Formula

SP = CP × (1 − Loss%)

Total Profit%

(Total SP − Total CP) ÷ Total CP × 100

Key Tip

Find CP per unit first for easier calculation
